candidate.name: MATCHING_LEAN_KERNEL_INVARIANT
candidate.semantics: Apply matching-autarky reduction to canonical normal form; clauses removed by an autarky are satisfiability-irrelevant to the residual decision instance.
candidate.exactness: F is satisfiable iff its matching-lean kernel N_ML(F) is satisfiable.
candidate.computability: The largest matching-lean sub-clause-set / matching-lean kernel is computable in polynomial time by matching-autarky reduction.
candidate.strict_progress_when_reducible: If a nontrivial matching autarky exists, at least one clause is removed while preserving satisfiability equivalence.

published_basis: Oliver Kullmann, Lean clause-sets: generalizations of minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets, Discrete Applied Mathematics 130(2), 2003, DOI 10.1016/S0166-218X(02)00406-7.

Matching autarkies admit a confluent/canonical reduction; matching-lean clause-sets are characterized by deficiency/surplus conditions and the largest matching-lean sub-clause-set is polynomial-time computable.

universal_progress_test.criterion: Legend-grade progress would require every nonterminal arbitrary 3CNF to admit a strict polynomial-time reduction step or an exact terminal decision.
universal_progress_test.reason: There are arbitrarily large satisfiable and unsatisfiable matching-lean formulas, so I_ML can equal F with no reduction while SAT status remains nontrivial.

explicit_sat_obstruction_family.base_gadget: G(x,y)={(x OR y),(NOT x OR y),(x OR NOT y)}
matching_lean_proof: G has c=3 clauses, n=2 variables, hence deficiency delta(G)=1.
Every one-clause proper subset has deficiency -1 because it contains two variables.
Every two-clause proper subset has deficiency 0.
Thus every proper F' subset G satisfies delta(F')<delta(G); by the standard matching-lean characterization, G is matching-lean.
explicit_sat_obstruction_family.infinite_family: S_k is the disjoint union of k variable-disjoint copies of G.
infinite_family_proof: S_k is satisfiable by satisfying each copy independently.
Any proper sub-clause-set contains at most k-1 complete gadgets; every incomplete gadget contributes deficiency <=0, hence delta(F')<=k-1<k.
Therefore S_k is matching-lean for every k>=1 and I_ML(S_k)=S_k.

explicit_unsat_obstruction_family.definition: U_n={x1, (NOT x1 OR x2), ..., (NOT x_{n-1} OR xn), NOT xn} for n>=1.
explicit_unsat_obstruction_family.width: at most 2, hence also within width-at-most-3 CNF
explicit_unsat_obstruction_family.unsat_proof: The first clause forces x1=true; each implication forces xi=true successively; the last clause forces xn=false.
explicit_unsat_obstruction_family.minimal_unsat_proof: Removing the first or last clause obviously restores a satisfying endpoint assignment; removing implication i permits x1..xi=true and x_{i+1}..xn=false, satisfying all remaining clauses.
explicit_unsat_obstruction_family.matching_lean_consequence: Every minimally unsatisfiable clause-set is lean and therefore matching-lean; hence I_ML(U_n)=U_n for every n.

derived_TRUMP_result.useful_role: Admit I_ML as a safe preprocessing/inprocessing invariant in JANUS/TRUMP, with zero Legend authority once the matching-lean kernel is reached.

next_admissible_math.requirement: A successor invariant must escape the S_k and U_n obstruction families by proving strict progress or exact terminal authority on them without reducing to previously blocked proof-search, local propagation, full-function compilation, explicit SoS, or generic PTIME-host relabeling.
